candidates.name: Run
candidates.reason: The run list and run detail need it: one record per capture, from the manifest and the a11y rollup.

candidates.name: Finding
candidates.reason: The finding list and finding detail need it: one rule failing on one page, from the page evidence (6 on this run).

candidates.name: Evidence
candidates.reason: What Stage1 calls evidence is, in its records, a file the run wrote — a kind, a path, bytes, a written-at and a sha256 the manifest attests. The run detail needs its artifact roster. Named for what it is; see the naming decision.

candidates.name: Artifact
candidates.reason: The same records as the above. Stage1 lists Evidence and Artifact separately, but on disk both are report-index entries under one manifest hash map; one object, not two.

candidates.name: Surface
candidates.reason: No screen this sprint shows a page on its own. Each finding names its route, page url and evidence file; the run states its page count (40). Born when a page screen is needed.

candidates.name: Subject
candidates.reason: Every run read carries exactly one target ({name, url}); on the run it is two fields. A Subject object is warranted only when a screen compares runs of one subject over time.

candidates.name: Comparison
candidates.reason: No two-run screen this sprint. Forge's comparison of a run with its own composition is Sprint 204's observation record, which already exists and is not an object.

artifacts.description: Accessibility scan findings and compliance details.
App profile summary of routes and related artifacts.
Baseline UX metrics derived from computed styles.
Responsive breakpoint detection with scale pattern analysis.
What the site lets a user DO, per capability, rolled up across surfaces with the evidence for each.
UI component clusters with variant and nesting detection.
A stable structural fingerprint per component, so the same component is recognisable across pages and across runs.
Recurring component compositions — which components habitually appear together, and in what arrangement.
Where the live site and the design system disagree — by value (colours, radii, type), by presence (components), and by naming.
Pseudo-entities INFERRED from URL route segments because no API scan ran — a placeholder product model, not a measured one. Its source_endpoints are page paths, not endpoints.
Information architecture outline with route taxonomy.
Entity mentions found on each surface before resolution — the raw material the identity graph joins.
Which entities on different surfaces are the SAME entity — the resolved cross-surface identity, with the evidence for each join.
What objects the site behaves as if it has — the product model inferred from IA and DOM structure alone, before any API evidence.
Per-object summary across the run: where each object appears, what it is called on each surface, and what evidence supports it.
Candidate objects, traits and relationships extracted from the capture — the input to inference, not its verdict.
Modals, banners, toasts and interstitials the site shows over its own content — the messaging layer a crawl usually misses.
Performance audit results and lighthouse metrics.
Where the observed UI and the declared design-system intent line up, and where they do not — per component, with what was matched against.
Index of artifacts produced in this run.
What a human needs to decide, ranked — the proposals this run is not confident enough to apply on its own.
Design token fingerprint extracted from UI styles.
The CSS rules as authored, per page — the evidence behind breakpoint, theming and token analysis.
Surface snapshot capturing DOM and visual context.
Theming and dark mode detection with CSS custom property analysis.
Design token guesses mapped to standard vocabulary.
Draft UI component manifest generated from observations.
